details: @c1-ease/commerce is a 4-file "compatibility shim" that implements no commerce functionality: index.js exports a Proxy of no-op functions and its only real action is an install-time callback. package.json declares a postinstall hook running beacon.cjs, and index.js invokes the same beacon again on require. beacon.cjs sends an HTTPS POST to hxxps://vmi3699893[.]contaboserver[.]net:8787/_ah/dc with an x-beacon-package header and a JSON body containing the package name, the machine hostname, the install path (__dirname), the current working directory and the npm/Node version. The request sets rejectUnauthorized:false, so it accepts any TLS certificate presented by that host on port 8787. The code reads no file contents, environment values,.npmrc, source-control or cloud tokens, SSH/AWS credentials or wallet data, and installs no second stage or persistence. The package README describes itself as an authorized dependency-confusion test beacon, but the callback target is a bare VPS endpoint with certificate verification disabled and the package otherwise performs no function. @c1-ease/commerce ships a postinstall hook ("node beacon.cjs"), and importing the package also fires that beacon from index.js, so the callback happens at install time as well as at require time. The beacon POSTs JSON containing the package name, the machine hostname (os.hostname()), the install path (__dirname), the current working directory and the npm/Node version to hxxps://vmi3699893[.]contaboserver[.]net:8787/_ah/dc with an x-beacon-package header, with TLS certificate verification disabled (rejectUnauthorized:false) so the self-signed certificate of the bare VPS is accepted. index.js otherwise exports a no-op Proxy so imported properties resolve to no-op functions and the host build completes. Versions 1.0.1, 1.1.0 and 3.0.0 ship the same four files (beacon.cjs, index.js, package.json, README.md) calling the same endpoint. The README describes the package as an authorized dependency-confusion test that performs no operation other than reporting that it was installed. The beacon payload is limited to install host metadata; no environment variables, credential files, npm config or user files are read or transmitted.

cwes.name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
